data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Camelle is derived from the word 'gamal' which means camel. Camels were often used in the Bible for long journeys and carrying heavy loads. Camelle could be seen as a symbol of strength and endurance, serving those in need. The name Camelle carries the meaning “Young camel” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Camelle usually hope their child will grow to embody young camel and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: קמלה
in_hebrew.meaning: קמלה היא שם שפירושו נזר או שושנת המים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קמלה הוא שם שמקורו בשושנת המים או בנזר. הוא קשור למילה העברית 'קמל' שפירושו שושנת המים. השם מופיע בכתבי הקודש כסמל לטוהרה ורעננות. השם קמלה משמש גם כמטפור לתחיית המתים ולחיים חדשים בישו

in_greek.name: Καμέλλη
in_greek.meaning: Καμέλλη σημαίνει το λουλούδι του κάμπου ή το νερολουλούδι
in_greek.long_meaning: Καμέλλη προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'κάμπος' που σημαίνει 'καλλιέργεια' ή 'λουλούδι'. Ονομάζεται επίσης νερολουλούδι, σύμβολο αγνότητας και ανανέωσης. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το λουλούδι αναφέρεται ως σύμβολο της πνευματικής ανανέωσης και της αιώνιας ζωής

in_latin.name: Camella
in_latin.meaning: Camella significat flos campi seu lilium aquae
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Camella derivatur ex latino 'camellus', qui est flos campi. Etiam lilium aquae vocatur, significans puritatem et renovationem. In primitiva ecclesia christiana, flos iste habebatur pro signo resurrectionis et novae vitae in Christo

historical_references.reference: In the 6th century, a holy hermit named Camellus lived in Egypt. He was known for his asceticism and miracles. His name was later Latinized to Camellus and became popular among Christians in the Western world.

The 13th-century Italian poet Dante Alighieri, in his Divine Comedy, mentions a character named Camilla, who is a warrior maiden and a Christian saint. It's believed that Dante may have intended this Camilla to be a reference to Saint Camillus of Jericho, who is also known as Camellus, due to the similarity in their names.
